item.text: {"comments":"The clean review is confirmed by direct source comparison. The source asks whether, for every k ≠ 1, infinitely many natural numbers n satisfy 2^n ≡ k (mod n); the Lean statement has the same quantifier scope and predicate. The extended binder `∀ᵉ (k : ℤ) (k ≠ 1)` expands to `∀ k : ℤ, k ≠ 1 → ...`, and `Set.Infinite` correctly expresses infinitely many n. Allowing n = 0 or n = 1 does not change infinitude, since these contribute at most finitely many exceptional values. The cited module also builds successfully with `lake --wfail`.
